3555064:
Spiritscar

The Spiritscar is an enormous, trench-like rift located in the northern hills of Kaoling in Tian Xia. Over seven miles long and nearly 800 feet deep, Spiritscar was once the location of a monastery dedicated to Lady Nanbyo, the Widow of Suffering. Dating back to the days of Imperial Lung Wa, even before the formation of the rift, the area that would become the Spiritscar had long been associated with misery. When hobgoblin forces first attacked the monastery, the cultists of Lady Nanbyo triggered a massive earthquake that destroyed everyone and created the current rift. The Spiritscar is now haunted by the ghosts of both the cultists and the hobgoblin army that attacked them.⁠
18483154:
Gyanpad

Gyanpad is a mountain within the larger Lohaparbat Mountains of Vudra. It is most famous for the garuda monk Mahadev, who has meditated near its peak for over a decade. A small cult has developed around Mahadev to help keep his body nourished and alive, although they claim his spirit has already ascended to a higher plane and may be in the process of becoming a god. Mahadev's psychic emanations have also drawn monstrous yetis and wendigos to Gyanpad and the surrounding area.⁠
20306254:
Wracked Rock

The Wracked Rock is a stony structure in an abandoned block of buildings in the Precipice Quarter, inhabited not out of necessity but because they are drawn by the strange dreams that occur when sleeping near the obelisk. Thousands of years ago, a Rovagug cultist summoned a giant monster to destroy the city, but heroes managed to turn it to stone before it could ravage the neighborhood, killing it by shattering it into pieces. The only part that remained was this rock, a tusk protruding from the head that lies buried underground. After the earthquake a few decades ago, a small opening opened into the subsoil, from which all who have ventured never return. Rovagug cultists are often seen in the area, but since their violence doesn't spread beyond the block, the Knights of Lastwall see no reason to intervene.⁠
28372684:
Fangspire

Fangspire is one of the shelters of the Abendego Piercing created by the Knights of Salvation after the Eye of Abendego devastated the Sodden Lands.

The magically constructed tower of stone and metal has withstood the storms for centuries and remains in good condition. However, the storms have undermined its foundations, and as a result the tower leans over the sea at a dangerous angle.

Fangspire is the traditional domain of the largest of the region's boggard tribes. The constant warfare between the various boggard tribes ensures no tribe can claim the honour for very long.⁠
34169554:
Therassic Spire

The Therassic Spire, also known as the Great Library, is one of the oldest repositories of knowledge in all of Varisia. A cabal of librarians who worship Nethys, Irori and the Peacock Spirit cares for the tomes within, some of which are illegible due to their age. The structure rises six stories above and below, and because no knowledge is forbidden here, mages, paladins, and thieves pay handsomely for access to these books and the power they may contain.⁠

In recent years, the librarians have made contact with the caulborns of Xavorax, with whom they exchange information and maintain a relationship of mutual interest. In 4712 AR, the librarians sent mercenaries in search of the Shard of Gluttony, but after losing contact with them, they had to ask the Pathfinder Society for help in resolving the matter discreetly.⁠
39617284:
Claw Point

Claw Point is the northernmost point in Brevoy. It is located on the shores of the Lake of Mists and Veils and is just north of the beginning of the Icerime Peaks.⁠ While generally uninhabited, this escarpment of wind-eroded rock features a miserable stone bunker where a handful of mercenaries from House Lodovka are stationed each year. The outpost houses a significant magical item for communication—an emerald crystal ball—which allows scouts to alert the mages of Limstatic Academe in Winterbreak of any external threats. Thanks to this warning system, countless attempts to overtake Claw Point by Iobarian warlords have ended in mutual destruction at best. Alongside help from the Limstatic Academe, attacks are often halted by strangely unaccountable windstorms, avalanches, and hail.⁠
40604994:
Crooked Cove

Crooked Cove, often referred to as Crookcove or Crook Cove, is a small village on the southwest coast of Ravounel. It houses an abandoned observatory.⁠
43276224:
Vigil's Rest

Vigil's Rest is a small outpost near the border with the Whistling Plains in Avin Prefecture. The Taldan Horse offers no protection beyond this point, and at least one regiment can always be seen in the area. Although Vigil's Rest is not especially populated, the local market is well supplied as it is on a main trading route. In addition to the Taldan Horse, the Lion Blades have members at the outpost who interrogate a good number of caravan workers that arrive from Casmaron.⁠

Statue of Primarch Harvi

The Statue of Primarch Harvi, located in the Petal District, is one of the city's most famous public artworks, but not for a positive reason as it's considered the most ugly statue in all of Absalom. It depicts this Primarch from the Age of Enthronement on horseback during the Red Siege of 4499 AR, but his face makes him look more like he has a cold or intestinal problems than anything that inspires courage. The Conclave of Flowers seems to agree that it should be removed, but the problem is what to put in its place. Some want a statue of Lord Gyr and his fellow adventurers, including Lord Avid, of course. Others, associated with the Citizens' League, prefer a statue honoring the soldiers who fell in the city's many sieges. And the new nobles want to improve their reputation with the Vault of Abadar by erecting a statue of Abadar.⁠
88072334:
Wyrmwatch

Both a functioning lighthouse and a tribute to Magnimar's founder Alcaydian Indros the Wyrmwatch, or Wyrmwatch Tower, is a one of the city's most prominent landmarks. The Wyrmwatch sits at the western most edge of Outcast's Cove at the very tip of Beacon's Point jutting out into the Varisian Gulf warning ships away from the dangerous spur of rock and welcomes them to the busy harbour of the Dockway and the Bazaar of Sails.

It supposedly sits upon the very site where Alcaydian Indros slew the mighty Sea Dragon known as Vydrarch which was one of the events that lead to the founding of Magnimar.⁠
140555254:
Hvorsuli

Hvorsuli, also known as the "Snow Spires", is a ruined city of thin spires and massive gates located within a glacier in northern Iobaria. Only the foremost gatehouse and a few broken domes lie outside the glacier and allow treasure hunters and explorers access to the ruins. The creators of the city are unknown, but there are mentions of a great power that glows in the heart of the city, contained by the ice god Rheth.⁠
141649144:
Longacre

The town of Longacre in central Cheliax stands on the Fields of Chelam near the western edge of the Whisperwood⁠ and forms the regional centre of the Archbarony of Longacre within the Archduchy of the Heartlands.⁠ Some believe that it is a gathering place for Chelaxian military veterans who have been censured for openly (or privately) criticizing the government or House Thrune.⁠

156982394:
Crystal Palace

The Crystal Palace was the palace of Xin, founder of Thassilon, and the site of his death and location of his remains. Upon his death, the Palace itself became infused with his restless spirit. It is located inside of a mountainous spire of crystal at the city of Xin, on an island about 100 miles west of Magnimar⁠ in what was formerly the southern coast of the Thassilonian realm of Bakrakhan.⁠

The Palace sank along with the rest of the island upon which the city of Xin was located during Earthfall, and it remained on the floor of the Arcadian Ocean until parts of the island were raised by adventurers in 4712 AR.⁠
158872434:
Red Drake Warehouses

Red Drake Warehouses is a series of warehouses in The Docks run by Ptarnex Dexarion, the ruthless boss of Ogrekin Hall. He runs the business by offering merchants space to store whatever they want, with the caveat that if they fail to pay for even a single month, all the merchandise inside becomes his property. He makes sure his customers are aware of this situation and has made more money selling confiscated goods than renting the space. It is said that he uses infernal contracts and hired thieves to steal from merchants so they can't pay on time, but since the rent is so low, many take the risk.⁠
176932474:
Windarium

The Windarium is a clockworks shop in Westgate that is going through difficult times. The shop is located in a shopping district frequented by those looking for parts or repairs. Founded by Symo in 4705 AR, the shop began to gain popularity when he met Mirtion, who had already successfully run several shops. In 4710 AR, they married, and Symo was promoted in 4716 AR. The shop's popularity was booming, and everything was going great. After the Black Echelon Uprising of 4717 AR, Symo was promoted again, and with no time for the shop, Mirtion has had to run it alone. He has no idea about the engineering required to maintain clockworks and, demotivated, has put his passion into the badgers who fill the shop and generate complaints about the bribes they take from customers and employees alike.⁠
188300964:
Aulamaxa Estate

Aulamaxa Estate, located in The Greens district of Kintargo, Ravounel, is the home of House Aulamaxa.⁠⁠
193801014:
Boria's

Boria's is an innocuous-looking wine shop on Lemnius Lane⁠ in the northern Naos district of the Varisian city of Magnimar, and is run by Todoban Boria. Numerous types of wholly unremarkable wines are displayed around the shop and a small statue of Cayden Cailean stands upon the front counter, all giving the impression of a perfectly ordinary establishment that sells wines. The truth is that Boria's is the city's premier supplier of poisons, manufactured or procured by the owner, and sold to a very selective clientele. Only with the proper references (such as from the Night Scales) does Boria display his true wares. The poison maker earns enough money from his illegal trade that he doesn't have to actually sell any wine. Because of this, Boria only makes enough of an effort to move his legal inventory so as not to arouse suspicion.⁠
193815144:
Seventh Church of Iomedae

The Seventh Church of Iomedae is an important temple of goddess in the Ascendant Court district of Absalom, and the site of the seventh of Iomedae's 11 miraculous acts, the calling of the Undying Light.⁠ This miracle is commemorated by the temple itself and the Iomedaenne, a 10-foot statue of the goddess carved from red limestone and banded with sapphires. Although the goddess is popular in the city, and the Seventh Church trains most of her clerics here for three or four years, most of the priests at the church are young or elderly, since her most vital followers take up service elsewhere. Absalom is seen as a place of recruitment by the goddess's church, rather than a bulwark of faith in peril. The high priest of the temple is Tavorae Falsebane, who replaced the aged Genedair the Faithful who passed on to his final reward. Across the main street from the church is the Tempering Hall, which trains paladins of Iomedae, as well those of the churches of Abadar, Irori, and Shelyn.⁠⁠
215477734:
Cypher Lodge

The Cypher Lodge in Riddleport is the headquarters of the Order of Cyphers.⁠ It is a combination of library, laboratory, research hall, and museum where cyphermages pursue the secrets of Thassilon.⁠
231910364:
Sianovel Agency

The Sianovel Agency is a consultancy and detective agency located in Erdan Sianovel's house in Westgate. It's sandwiched between a bakery and a woodworking shop, with an eye-catching window display. Erdan is already incredibly wealthy, so his clients' ability to pay isn't as important as the cases they bring him; he only takes on the most interesting ones. Lady Seleenae is one of his most regular clients, serving as both his boss and friend and the business also deals in antiques, though it doesn't buy or sell stolen goods. Chirrup Turley is the shop's secretary, managing the business when Erdan is working at the Foreign Coin Exchange.⁠
246432594:
Palin's Cove

Named for Keyra Palin, naval heroine of early Korvosa, Palin's Cove is one of the most important holdings of the city-state's realm. Originally a military outpost, Palin's Cove played a vital role in early Chelaxian victories over the Shoanti. Located approximately 80 miles northwest of Korvosa at the mouth of the Falcon River, Palin's Cover served as a naval garrison until 4485 AR, when it became an official settlement of the city.⁠

Over the years, a number of extensive Shoanti sieges were laid on the town, but it never fell, and was rewarded by Korvosa with a strong industrial presence. Modern-day Palin's Cove can be identified for miles around by the cloud of thick black smoke which rises from its many factories. The pollution caused by the industrial epicenter of the town have caused great animosity and even violence from druids, Gozreh worshipers, and even ordinary smiths and craftsmen pushed out of their niche in the market by the overwhelming workhouses.⁠

Not only do the catapults, ballistae, and trebuchets it produces serve as major exports both for the town and Korvosa, but they remain ever ready for another attack, a remnant of the town's military origins.⁠ Despite these defenses, Palin's Cove has long been plagued by the red dragon Glarataxus, who has periodically tormented the town since his first attack in 4571.⁠
258615954:
Baldachin

Baldachin is a small town at the mouth of the Frozen Road on Glacier Lake in the Irriseni capital province of Thronehold.⁠
261166494:
Alendruan Harbor

Founded by the elven witch called Kaala Raingold around 4622 AR, Alendruan Harbor is as of 4712 AR the main port on the Shackles' island of Kepre Dua.⁠
265031114:
Androsphinx of Zukebri

The Androsphinx of Zukebri is an ancient monument in Osirion's Underdunes in the form of a sphinx, with a bronze-cast face of an unknown pharaoh and massive ruby and sapphire adornments. Powerful magic protects it from the Underdunes' constantly shifting sands and leaves it at the center of a perfectly circular crater of flat ground, and any who approach it are assaulted by its piercing telepathic screams similar to mind quakes. The monument also seems to weep tears of unknown black fluid.⁠⁠⁠

A cult of Lamashtu, comprised of the rare people unaffected by its telepathic attacks and possibly inspired by another Lamashtan cult near Eto, worships the monument and has sacrificed travelers who draw near.⁠⁠ Occult researchers have attempted to link the androsphinx to the 11 gifts reportedly given to the Four Pharaohs by "Emissaries" from Aucturn in the Calosian Manuscript.⁠
273517164:
Courtesan and Unicorn

The Courtesan and Unicorn is a combination harrow parlor and brothel run by Vanyavi Czanji in the Lowcleft district of Magnimar. The harrow readings are often performed by non-Varisians dressed up as a caricature of true members of this ethnicity. Shoanti guards fanatically loyal to Czanji monitor the premises. Their pay consists of credit with the prostitutes.⁠
276856384:
Dread Dungeons

High in the Fog Peaks of Galt is a building with a dark past, even by the blood-soaked standards of this anarchic nation. Built to house political prisoners and other undesirables, soon after its construction it was discovered that its deepest cells connected to tunnels that led even further below into the Darklands. The building built in 4687 AR⁠ by a temporary government known as the Galtcreed Pact was named Galtcreed, but the deep tunnels and cells below were eventually named the Dread Dungeons. Some of the cells are infested with dangerous cytillesh fungus.

Primarch Bremovir, one of the leading lights of the Galtcreed Pact, allied himself with the dero of Kmlin-Bru, using them to seize dissidents from their beds and also to serve as some of the prison guards. The staff at the prison remained loyal to Bremovir, and he was able to flee here when the Galtcreed Pact was overthrown as part of Galt's endless cycle of revolution. Successive governments have tried to discover the prison's location, but without success.

Numerous prisoners were executed in the prison, and others have been taken by the dero for their warped experiments, but a considerable number still remain. It is rumoured that amongst their number is a prisoner who could bring lasting peace to troubled Galt—the guards will not kill him but also dare not let him escape.⁠⁠
277065704:
Uddo

Uddo was the capital of the Teikoku Shogunate in what is now known as Minkai. It was conquered and razed by the armies of Kuga Setsuna during the Battle of Eight Bridges in 6116 IC; Minkai was founded three years later, with the downriver port city of Kasai as its capital.⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠
282101354:
Scrapwall

Scrapwall is a town⁠ in the Sellen Hills built out of a gigantic technological junkyard almost three miles in length. Having never had a formal leader in its thousands of years of history, the city is instead run by disparate rival gangs.⁠⁠
290889204:
Kintargo Opera House

The Kintargo Opera House in the city of Kintargo, Ravounel, is beloved by the local population and has been the stage for such famous soloists as Shensen.⁠⁠ It is one of the most esteemed opera venues in Avistan.⁠
297314784:
Whistledown

The town of Whistledown is one of the few settlements in Varisia not affiliated with either Korvosa or Magnimar, though it is located almost exactly halfway between the two larger cities. Founded at the western edge of the Fenwall Mountains, where Lake Syrantula flows back into the Yondabakari River, the town is known primarily as the heart of the gnome population in Varisia, despite the fact that it contains just as many humans as gnomes. Nevertheless, much of the town's buildings and its white-walled cottages are sized for gnomes. Its name derives from the strange wooden charms which produce haunting melodies in the night winds off the lake, and this nightly music tends to put off most non-gnome visitors.⁠⁠
302426694:
Candlestone Caverns

The Candlestone Caverns are a vast labyrinth of living limestone tunnels and caves located in the northeastern Aspodell Mountains of Andoran near the border with Cheliax. They were exposed only two centuries ago in an earthquake.⁠ Deep below the Candlestone Caverns is the Endless Gulf, a rift in Golarion's crust that connects to the Darklands realms of Nar-Voth, Sekamina, and Orv.⁠

Carpenden (sometimes spelled Carpendren⁠) is the most influential city in the Carpenden region of Andoran. Located on the north-central Carpenden Plains, it is surrounded by rolling hills that lend themselves to the creation of numerous plantations and orchards.⁠⁠
345504324:
Nightshade Theater

Nightshade Theater is a stone structure that, from the outside, resembles a cathedral dedicated to some malevolent god more than a theater, but inside it boasts silk carpets, paintings of macabre scenes, and seating for around 250 people. 347486184:
Okerra Estate

Okerra Estate is home to Nicolaus Okerra as well as his daughter Selli Okerra and serves as the seat of House Okerra. It is a small and cozy citadel, especially when compared with nearby estates like the Palace of Birdsong, that sits overlooking the town of Pensaris.⁠
352064794:
Shatterglass

Shatterglass is a small and picturesque village located in the north-easternmost corner of the nation of Mendev, on the shore of the Lake of Mists and Veils.⁠ The village's name is derived from the shimmering lake glass that blankets its shores.⁠

The settlement is primarily inhabited by retired pirates, and the entire village is constructed from lumber salvaged from ships. The carpenters of Shatterglass are meticulous in choosing the source of their materials and prefer using the hulls of famous pirate ships for construction, even though many of these buildings have a reputation for being haunted.⁠

Humbolt's Outfitters

Humbolt's Outfitters is a general store run by the merchant Gron Humbolt in The Coins and thanks to his wife, Lady Myleena, it has gained a great reputation in recent years. It occupies two floors in a stone structure that could easily be mistaken for a fortress, were it not for the arches, crates, and shelves inside, overflowing with all sorts of items.⁠ From clothing and tools to rations, the store has absolutely everything one could possibly need, whether for adventures in the Immenwood or climbing in the Kortos Mounts; if it exists, it's here. By Gron's rule, no magical items are sold in the store, directing customers to the Arcanamirium or his friend Engleton Embrey if they require such things. His wife sometimes works, mostly behind the scenes, and thanks to her support, they have been able to open satellite stores in the Foreign Quarter and Westgate.⁠
383905434:
Djeneg

Djeneg is a village in the Footprints of Rovagug area of Osirion. It is located near the mineral spring known as The Great Pool. The Great Pool has been visited by Osirian nobles for millennia, and the village of Djeneg grew up around the pool to support its visitors.⁠
391193824:
Citadel Vaull

Citadel Vaull, located in the Castle District of the city of Kintargo in Ravounel, housed the otherwise nomadic Hellknight Order of the Torrent until 4715 AR, when new Lord-Mayor Barzillai Thrune stripped the order of its charter and had the Order of the Rack loot the citadel of its contents.⁠⁠

After Barzillai Thrune was removed from power and Kintargo and Ravounel won their independence from Cheliax in 4716 AR, Citadel Vaull was returned to the Order of the Torrent, who began renovating its facade to be more approachable. However, work has been slowed by the Order's simultaneous work caring for Castle Kintargo.⁠

Vangeline Pass

The Vangeline Pass in the Shattered Range provides entrance into a remote portion of western Geb from the eastern Mwangi Expanse.⁠ It is one of the three major passes from the Mwangi Expanse to the east: Kho-Rarne Pass, the Ndele Gap, and the Vangeline Pass. Tanadesh

Tanadesh is an unusual mahajanapada in the Cradle region of Vudra. Unlike most mahajanapadas composed of Vudrani, Tanadesh is a kingdom of vishkanyas, humanoids who possess a supernatural affinity for poison and guile. It is a jungle kingdom located toward the centre of the Cradle.⁠

455306014:
Botosani

The Rahadoumi city of Botosani is located on the Arcadian Ocean on the west coast of the Kingdom of Man.

As with the rest of the nation, religion is completely banned in the city but persistent rumors of a cult of Iomedae have recently gained enough credence to be considered a threat, resulting in an increase in activity among the Pure Legion. The ongoing famine besetting Botosani makes fully devoting the resources needed difficult for the Legion, however, and they now look for outside help to either rout the cult by force or to create a public spectacle which they could then clean up.

Famine and cults are not the only threats to the well-being of Botosani, though, as three times in the last half century the city has been the victim of a terrible plague and pirates from the nearby Shackles continue to make trouble for the nation's navy and trading vessels going to and from the busy port. Being the major Rahadoumi port nearest the Eye of Abendego, where the pirates often flee for refuge, it is here that able seamen and naval guides are most in demand to help track down and dispatch the seafaring threats.⁠
485390504:
Sostarlannex

Sostarlannex is an annex between the Canal Wisxar and the Canal Thrachi, featuring a grimy wall which still retains the bas-reliefs depicting the exploits of the Great Drought, sculpted by Sostarl.⁠
509769024:
Throne of the Troll King

The Throne of the Troll King is a huge stone chair atop a high hill near the Kodar Mountains, which is located in the Southmoor region of the Lands of the Linnorm Kings. Legends claim that by sitting on the throne overnight at midwinter, one could gain dominion over all of Southmoor's trolls until the following midwinter's eve. Consequently, dozens of troll tribes guard the area around the throne to ensure that nobody attempts to prove the legend true.⁠

Fortunately for the trolls, the legends are just that, legends, and the preservation magic of many of the monuments of Thassilon is what has keep the throne in perfect shape for such a long time. In the past, it was a rune giant who commanded the obedience of the lesser giants of the region from here; and that was because of their innate ability to command giants and not because the throne had any power.⁠
515932234:
Ullerskad

Ullerskad is an Ulfen city situated on the northern banks of the Rimeflow River in the Lands of the Linnorm Kings. It is a major settlement in the region known as the Thanelands and a hub of trade and commerce in the region. Many of the wealthiest Ulfen live in the city, which is known for its popularity among retired Huscarls of the Ulfen Guard who have returned from their well-paid services to the emperor of Taldor.

Numerous hunting lodges dot the surrounding region, and hunting the local wild boars (and the troublesome wolves that prey on the farmers' flocks) is a popular pastime.

Ullerskad is the location of a gold-adorned temple to Gorum. The nearby stream and grove of trees is the site of sacrifice, especially during the spring equinox.⁠
520896034:
Blood Fountain

The Blood Fountain is a Ghol-Gan ruin on the island of Dahak's Tooth in the Shackles. A magical cistern stands at the center of the ancient ruined settlement. The cistern appears to be fully functional, save that red, bilious liquid constantly pours from it, seeping into the ground around it and ensuring that no flora grows there.⁠
524506674:
Eto

Eto is the largest city of central Osirion, located just north of the mountain range known as the Pillars of the Sun. It sits at the crossing of numerous overland trade routes, including the major one between Sothis to the east and Shiman-Sekh to the west, and has seen its fortunes wax with the increase of foreign trade since Osirion's independence. In addition to benefiting from this increased trade, it has also become a launching pad for adventurers seeking to plunder the country's many ancient tombs.⁠
549001304:
Mirnbay

First founded in 1528 AR, Mirnbay is a vibrant and prosperous port city. Protected by palisades and located on a peaceful lagoon of the Castrovin Sea near the mouth of the Myrfrus River,⁠ Mirnbay is the largest and most peaceful city in the land of Iobaria.

Along with several other nearby humanoid settlements, Mirnbay was sacked in 1900 AR by the united centaur tribes of the Caemorin, under the banner of Errindayn the Seer. Mirnbay was later refounded in 2108 AR with its defences significantly strengthened, and centaurs were banned from the city for the next 400 years. With New Iobaria's collapse in 4659 AR, Mirnbay became one of last remaining power centres in the region.

Mirnbay's 22 noble houses rule the port city through a labyrinthine political system based on careful alliances and strategies. This system has faced disruption from the recent influx of Galtan nobility fleeing that nation's revolution. As of 4710 AR, Galtans controlled more than a third of the city's trade guilds, as well as five of the 22 noble houses. The city is led by an alliance of House Rhukov, a breakaway faction of the Iobarian royal House Arjal that controls the wizards of the city's arcane college, and House Xsagi, which controls Mirnbay's military.⁠

Dragon-Eel Port

Located near where the Silkstring River meets the Sea of Eels,⁠ the Hu clan's enclave of Dragon-Eel Port coordinates Songbai's maritime trade over the inland sea. The prices of the nation's commodities are discussed here between representatives of the Songbai Shogunate, the Four Notables and, most recently, advisors from Goka.⁠
560684914:
New Towne

New Towne is the most rundown settlement in the Meratt County region of Taldor. It is made up of the former inhabitants of Jambis, who fled the now-ruined settlement and live in squalid conditions, with many residents inhabiting little more than tents. The residents are still technically under the protection of House Telus, but the last baron, Araig Telus, has been absent for at least a decade.⁠

After fleeing Jambis, many of the residents settled in an area that looked promising for farming. The soil was poor, however, and New Towne has struggled to support itself since being founded about a decade prior to 4718 AR.

As of that year, the settlement was led by Tribune Caphridius Vort, who is considered to be a good man but more interested in opera and finery than rulership and far out of his depth.⁠ An aiuvarin upstart named Felsha has been advocating on behalf of New Towne to anyone who will listen.⁠
580111394:
Muliwan

Muliwan (pronounced MULL-one)⁠ is one of only two permanent settlements in the nomadic nation of Hongal, in Tian Xia. It is positioned at the southern end of the nation, with the capital of Ordu-Aganhei at the northern end.⁠⁠⁠
582445934:
Mirivenn

Mirivenn is a settlement of aquatic elves in the Arcadian Ocean, located a few hundred miles off the coast of Ravounel west of the Dismal Nitch.⁠
585720504:
Silvertree

Silvertree is a small settlement in northwestern Vidrian. Under the rule of Sargava, it was known as Crown's End.⁠
586210654:
Vauntil

The small town of Vauntil is located in the Ustalavic province of Caliphas on Lake Encarthan's Avalon Bay.⁠⁠ The settlement is notable for its skilled folk artisans, fierce competition for noble patronage, flowers, and good food and wine.⁠

The town is perhaps the most scenic and affluent regions in the county, largely due to the miles of vineyards and flower farms surrounding the settlement. Each year, chefs, vintners, perfumers, jewelers, and artists of all walks compete in the annual "Last Breath" festival for the highly coveted mantle "Worth Dying For". The competition is mired in regular tragedies and scandals including the use of human ingredients, assassinations, and mysterious deaths. Modern participants are unperturbed by this disasters, giving the competition a dangerous reputation and a morbid theme which has served to heighten its infamy.⁠

Vauntil was the location where troops of the Shining Crusade established a beachhead in their war against Tar-Baphon in 3801 AR.⁠
587154524:
Emerald Spire

The Emerald Spire is a strange ruin in the northwestern River Kingdoms. Located in a large clearing in the Echo Wood near the Crusader Road, six miles northeast of the Hellknight-ruled settlement of Fort Inevitable, the spire is well known to locals and travellers in the region.⁠

Believed to be an Azlanti ruin from the era before Earthfall, most think the Emerald Spire refers to the ruins of large tower of green glass that rises above the clearing. However, the spire itself is far more ancient, a needle of magical crystal that reaches two miles into the earth, into the very vaults of Orv.⁠
591258094:
Qumarin

The remnants of the lost and accursed city of Qumarin are located in the southern Meraz Desert of Qadira. Its location has been largely forgotten except for a few reclusive girtablilu tribes and it is avoided by everyone.⁠⁠⁠

Monastery of the Seven Forms

The Monastery of the Seven Forms is an underground city built around a Tian monastery, located in the prefecture of Whitemarch in the nation of Taldor. This settlement is nestled in the World's Edge Mountains, and overlooks the lands of the empire all the way to the Inner Sea.⁠
628945884:
Eel's Skull

The Eel's Skull is a disused fortress in the Shackles. It is situated on Nalt's Island located between Bag Island and Shark Island,⁠ standing at the edge of a sheer cliff on the northern expanse of the island's eastern shore.⁠

At one time it was the fortress home of the notorious pirate Nalt Tarbrow. It is said that there are Ghol-Gan dungeons beneath the fortress, but Tarbrow destroyed the fortress in a fit of madness, and no entrance to any dungeon has been found in the ruins.⁠ Yet the lowest levels of Eel's Skull still hide an entrance to the ancient Ghol-Gani region of the Darklands known as the Sleepless Realm.⁠ The ruins are still visible from the ships passing and every sailor knows that wealth lies somewhere deep within the cursed castle's abandoned halls and caverns.⁠

Only two adventurers are known to have emerged from the dread dungeons of Eel's Skull alive and both were terribly altered by the experience. No attempts restore either to full health or sanity. Their eyes remained blind and pupil-less, their skin remained ash white and they continued to tremor. One eventually killed himself by setting himself on fire (as Nalt's own fiery end), while the other, a Pathfinder named Gelrue Palane, is last rumored to have set off for Besmara's Throne.⁠

Morta's Mortuary

Morta's Mortuary is the main funeral home in the Isgeri town of Breachill. The building is painted black and black curtains are draped in every window. Numerous paintings and decorations of psychopomps fill the building, as its owner, Morta Valaskin, has an affinity for such outsiders.⁠

Scarwall

The immense gothic fortress of Scarwall is located in the far-eastern reaches of the Kodar Mountains within the Hold of Belkzen.⁠

Hope's Hollow

The quiet agricultural town of Hope's Hollow is an hour's ride along the eastern road from the city of Cassomir in Taldor, through the Blackwood Swamp.⁠
675327014:
Kembe

The ruins of Kembe are in the southern part of the Mwangi Jungle, in the Mwangi Expanse.⁠

It consists of three concentric rings of buildings. The buildings of the inner ring are sized for giants, those of the middle ring are sized for humans, and those of the outer ring are sized for halflings.

According to the myths carved on the city walls, a race of giants arrived from the sky in silver craft. They built the inner ring of buildings, but over generations found themselves getting smaller and smaller, requiring the building of the middle ring, and then finally the outer ring. They eventually shrunk too small to be seen.⁠

682858524:
Three Stars

The Three Stars are a set of three pyramids in southeastern Katapesh, within 20 miles of the Katapeshi coastline and Obari Ocean. The pyramids are made of yellow stone and topped with a large shining crystal that supposedly repairs itself if damaged.

Each pyramid is only 12 feet tall, small when compared with Katapeshi sites like the Red Pyramid or the Glass Pyramids and tiny when compared with Osirion's vast structures. There are no known entrances to the pyramids, and they are subject to the usual rumors suggesting that the pyramids hide either a dragon's horde, a dead king's treasure, or undead genies.

One of the more unusual and most prominent rumors is that the pyramids hide the remains of some sort of benevolent being described as either beings of living flame, beautiful maidens, or feathered serpents (possibly describing a muse azata) who sleeps beneath the pyramids.

The rumours also suggest that one day the sleepers will awaken. One such story claims that this will happen when Golarion becomes too chaotic, while according to another rumor there is a fourth pyramid that can be used to awaken the sleepers.⁠
691311744:
Palace of the People's Council

The many chambers of the Palace of the People's Council serve as the meeting places and offices of the People's Council, Andoran's legislative body. Located in the Liberty District, at the western end of the Field of Concord in the capital city of Almas, the ground floor of the palace contains a massive amphitheater packed with marble benches in which the council members meet to debate Andoren laws. The rest of the building is filled with the council members' offices and other personal spaces.⁠
693103804:
Sulfur Gulch

The Sulfur Gulch is a large module of an ancient spaceship that once stored toxic gases used for various ship functions. As of 4716 AR, it was slowly leaking the gases it contained, giving it its name.⁠
695577074:
Temple of An-Alak

The Temple of An-Alak is a site in desert of eastern Osirion. It is located between the Underdunes and the Salt Hills.⁠
696378404:
Wreck of the Paradise

The Wreck of the Paradise lies forty feet underwater in the Claybottom Lake. The ship served as a casino for the mysterious Lucrecia, but in 4707 AR it sank in a fire, and the skeletons of its dozens of patrons at the time are scattered throughout the area.⁠
696449654:
Sanqatada Cinqarda

The Sanqatada Cinqarda, the Cathedral of the Five Founders, is an immense cathedral dedicated to the five founders of Westcrown, which predates Cheliax and Andoran as provinces of the empire. The facade remains shining, refusing any attempt to deface it in any way.⁠ The 30-foot-tall limestone statues beside each doorway stand on Turanian greenstone columns and represent one of the founders: Dotara, Palmor, Rixana, Adel, and Crucisal.⁠
698423574:
Nisroch

Nisroch is the largest city in Nidal and also its most open. For most of the port's visitors, that means very little. The few ships that dock here are closely inspected, and the streets are heavily patrolled. Finding little in the way of traditional port entertainment, most foreigners spend as little time in the company of the city's suspicious inhabitants as possible.⁠
699022054:
Grog Pit

The Grog Pit is the most notorious tavern and flophouse in the Docks district of Absalom. It is a dangerous place serving sour drinks. One third of the patrons are either cutpurses or con artists.⁠

Its famous grog is simple a collection of whatever the owner can find to pour into a central open-topped barrel, including leftovers from customers' glasses, spoiled wine from resellers, and rotting hallucinogenic herbs steeped in seawater. However the grog is cheap (any coin of any nation gets you a large mug full), the virtue of the serving girls and busboys is up for rent, and anyone who buys a mug can sleep off its effects in the main hall for free.⁠

Large enough groups of sailors are usually safe and charitable priests occasionally pass through to cure the worst diseases present. Many merchants and captains have tried to close down the Grog Pit, but it is very popular with the dock workers and when the tavern gets closed down no goods move on or off the ships until it is reopened.⁠

The Pathfinder Osprey uses the Grog Pit as a secret rendezvous and briefing location due to it being so disgusting, any spies would likely keep away.⁠
707643234:
Rhet's Home

Rhet's Home is an orphanage in the northern part of Mudhaven. It appears to be an ordinary house, but the happy laughter of children playing in the yard can be heard. The dromaar Rhet Tafmar founded it and cares for the children with great dedication, finding them adoptive families and enjoying a very good reputation in the district. Some speculate that he must have been an orphan himself, but in reality, he is the son of a successful merchant from Katapesh who uses the funds generously given to him by his family to maintain the orphanage.⁠

Bacul Gruii

The village of Bacul Gruii was taken over by Petchki, a foreign merchant, who enslaved the locals to harvest wood and livestock for his band of mercenaries. Petchki's men slew Otok, the village chief, and mounted his head in the town square to keep the villagers afraid. Petchki pays the villagers next to nothing and only does so to avoid violating the fifth River Freedom prohibiting slavery. To legitimize his rule over Bacul Gruii, the mercenary captain plans to marry one of Otok's daughters and declare himself the new village chief.⁠
737763504:
Storasta

Storasta was once one of the greatest cities of the Kellid nation of Sarkoris in northeastern Avistan. Founded in 3844 AR, it was finally abandoned in 4644 AR⁠ like the rest of the Worldwound. During its occupation, Storasta was overrun by demons until it was freed at the end of the Fifth Mendevian Crusade.⁠⁠ Due to its complete corruption, however, the crusaders decided to raze the city rather than rebuild it.⁠
752236864:
Wounded Wisp

The Wounded Wisp is a tavern in the western Foreign Quarter of Absalom. Its proprietor and bartender is Heryn Gale, who inherited the establishment from her father. The Wisp was one of the bars at which the Pathfinder Society was founded on 23 Desnus, 4307 AR, and has served as an unofficial Society bar since.⁠⁠
773194024:
Glimmerhold

Glimmerhold is a small, independent dwarven city. As of 4715 AR, it had been located within the borders of the human country of Nirmathas, near its border at the time with Nidal and prior to the establishment of Oprak.⁠
785783874:
Castinlee

Castinlee is an agricultural settlement located in the Swardlands of the Isle of Kortos. It is known for the many orchards of productive fruit and nut trees in the area.⁠⁠
799857124:
Todorokaze

Todorokaze (pronounced toh-doh-roh-Kah-zeh)⁠ is one of the many cities that dot the tengu kingdom of Kwanlai. It is the only city in the Kimu Mountains and a throughpoint for travelers and caravans crossing the range, and also is home to Tian Xia's largest shrine to the tengu deity Hei Feng. Todorokaze is known for its volatile weather, which its structures harness through myriad use of lightning rods.⁠

The thieves' guild of Todorokaze is responsible for the Autumn of Iron Tears, a conflict with the thieves' guild of the city of Seidoyaji that escalated into a full-blown proxy war between the two cities.⁠
807805734:
Drownyard

The Drownyard is a location in the city of Absalom, in the (now mostly destroyed) Precipice Quarter.

Before the terrible earthquake of 4698 AR, the Precipice Quarter (formerly known as Beldrin's Bluff) was known as the Tri-Towers Yard, the premier finishing school for children of the rich and powerful. The unexpected quake destroyed the academy and the students within, but the quake also brought forth a spray from the sewer that contained the remains of an (previously unknown) ancient necropolis over which the school had been built. The lower reaches of the Drownyard access this old necropolis.⁠⁠

Now the Tri-Towers Yard is better known as the Drownyard, a desolate ruin filled with salty brine and haunted by undead. For a decade after the tragedy, the site has been off limits to outsiders, the families of the dead erecting a fence of black iron around the area to keep out morbid intruders and even archaeological groups. The Pathfinder Society was eventually permitted access to the area.⁠
819104854:
Vault of the Forgotten Prophet

The Vault of the Forgotten Prophet is a vault hidden under the plains of Rhuzam that can only be accessed by using teleportation magic.⁠
842091174:
Erran Tower

The Erran Tower is one of the aeon towers that Aroden placed around the Isle of Kortos.⁠ The tower is a 300-foot-tall mudbrick step pyramid with a flat top.⁠⁠

The tower is located on the east side of the Isle of Erran,⁠ and is responsible for magically giving life to the area.⁠
844388504:
Bartie's Barges

Bartie's Barges is a shipyard in The Docks run by halflings affiliated with Darabelle Fairwind's Pilot's Union. They typically build small, flat-bottomed boats.⁠
849054924:
Old City Hall

The Old City Hall is the former city hall of Korvosa, also colloquially known as the Charcoal Palace. The Old City Hall was, for a long time, the tallest building in all Varisia, only being beaten by the Arvensoar in the rival city of Magnimar. Old City Hall served for over sixty years but was replaced by the current City Hall in 4489 AR when Remsev Ornelos moved the government out of the Charcoal Palace.⁠
863873614:
Cenotaph

The Cenotaph is an ancient, monumentally large pillar of black rock which rises from a cliff on the southern tip of the Tusk Mountains in the Hold of Belkzen. The main feature of this enormous rock is the huge pair of fifty-foot-high doors that bar entrance to whatever lies within.⁠
878312114:
Fish Tank

Owned by Jaster Frallino, the head of the Magnimarian Sczarni gang known as the Gallowed, the Fish Tank bears images of glassy-eyed sea serpents and scandalously clad mermaids staring stupidly from this peeling sea-blue caravan wagon's timbers. Within, the roomy wagon holds a single battered stool and a four-foot-tall glass aquarium filled with murky water.

Inside the glass tank laze Frallino's three fat pet swamp barracudas: Verna, Argarno, and Big Mal. In Frallino's displeasure, several lazy thugs and untrustworthy business partners have lost a toe, a nose, or a whole hand to "The Boss's Fish," and more than one of the crimelord's enemies have gone into the tank head first. It is also rumored that the Sczarni boss keeps a collection of mysterious, rusted keys at the bottom of his chummy aquarium, guarded by his beloved pets.
880192944:
Hedgerow Holloway

Hedgerow Holloway is one of the most luxurious and comfortable inns in all of Greengold, where foreign dignitaries stay when they need lodging in the city. The surrounding gardens contain hedge mazes and statues of various animals, as well as beautiful fountains and benches where one can sit and relax.⁠
881767584:
Outsea

Outsea is a town in the River Kingdoms containing farmland, swampland, rivers, and canals. Its citizens include both aquatic species as well as air-breathers. Military service is mandated for all water-breathers and a few landlubbers serve in respected voluntary battalions. Locks and gates separate freshwater and salt water, preventing the districts from flowing into each other. Beneath the waterline, coral reefs and seaweed form underwater structures. Fish, octopuses, and other aquatic animals are prevalent. Mages of Outsea are known for their strong tradition of practicing water magic. Unique spells of merfolk and sedacthy origins can be found only in this kingdom.⁠

Flameford

Flameford is a small Shoanti camp near Kaer Maga.⁠

Remesiana

The Chelaxian city of Remesiana stands at the mouth of the Iseld River, where it flows out of the Whisperwood into the Bay of Solva and the Inner Sea.⁠ The Hellknights of the Order of the Nail were based at nearby Citadel Draythe before moving to Varisia at the urging of Queen Domina of Korvosa in 4682 AR.⁠ Like much of the southern coast of Cheliax, Remesiana is considered a stronghold of the old noble families who survived the Chelaxian Civil War. They now fight desperately to remain in the crown's good graces as they see their hereditary powers ebbing away.⁠

Nantambu


Nantambu, also called the Song-Wind City,⁠ is a colourful, cheerful city-state in the western Mwangi Expanse. A haven of peace, learning, and culture within the Expanse, it is home to the Magaambya, one of the oldest, if not the oldest arcane schools on Golarion.⁠
920672594:
Zolurket Mines

The Zolurket Mines, once called Tar-Urkatha, are played-out platinum mines. Zolurket is a Kelish word for "Dark Death".

Zolurket remains abandoned for two reasons: the lack of worthwhile ores and minerals, and the presence of undead predators. The types of undead that lurk in the mines are unknown. There are rumors that Zolurket was abandoned before its wealth was depleted,⁠⁠ and a mining company based in the city of Katapesh is attempting to reopen them.⁠
925741934:
Licktoad Village

The Licktoad Village was where the Licktoad goblins of Brinestump Marsh lived in huts. The atmosphere was foul, and since it blocked a road, they harassed travelers who tried to pass through the area. The leader of the tribe was Rendwattle Gutwad, who didn't speak because his deep voice would terrify his subjects.⁠
932324654:
Crestwatch

Crestwatch is a structure with a 100-foot minaret in the middle of The Docks that serves as the administrative center of the district. The east wing is used by the Harbor Guard, which patrols and fights crime, and the west wing is used by the Docks Council, which creates the laws and taxes that apply to ships docking in the harbor. There are tensions about having criminal elements in the same building as those who administer the port.⁠
938872444:
Ecanus

Ecanus is a fortress-city in southern Nex that was established during the centuries-long war with neighbouring Geb. It is a sprawling city that serves as the hub of Nex's arcane-powered military. Here the battle mages that make up the backbone of the army are trained in a mixture of potent evocation and battle tactics. The city is also famous for its fleshforges: building-sized artefacts created by the archmage Nex himself that provide the terrifying war beasts which support the battle mages. The fleshforges are responsible for many of the nightmarish creatures which roam the wastelands of Nex, the Barrier Wall mountains, the Mana Wastes, and even the Mwangi Expanse.⁠

The city is the terminus of a trade route that winds its way south through the Mana Wastes, ending at the Gebbite town of Graydirge.⁠
942412104:
Wise Dragon Inn

The Wise Dragon Inn caters primarily to university-associated guests and is located in the Heights District of Korvosa.⁠⁠
943912664:
Dhucharg

Dhucharg is the capital of the hobgoblin nation of Kaoling in northwestern Tian Xia, and is by far the most impressive of all the country's cities.⁠⁠
952006334:
Citadel Gheisteno

Citadel Gheisteno was the headquarters of the Order of the Crux, a now defunct order of mercenaries who claimed to be Hellknights. The order refused to disband after the Chelaxian Civil War and was destroyed by the Order of the Scourge in Desnus 4663 AR.⁠⁠ The castle too was put to the torch, and it stood for over 50 years as a charred reminder to those who might oppose the Hell-inspired proponents of absolute law.⁠⁠

In 4688 AR, a grim parody of the former fortress reappeared along with three undead graveknights who called themselves the Order of the Crux, and began to gather an army of deathless soldiers around them.⁠⁠⁠
956278914:
Kravenkus

The dwarven hold of Kravenkus stands in the World's Edge Mountains, in Taldor. It is one of the original Sky Citadels, and still maintains a connection to the Darklands.⁠

Like the other Sky Citadels, Kravenkus was built by the dwarves soon after their Quest for Sky as a fortress from which to continue their epic war against the orcs. Kravenkus is one of the four remaining in dwarven hands.⁠

Kravenkus is something of a ghost town, consisting of around 2,500 dwarves protected by a small garrison of only 400. The inhabitants typically reside in the central "keep" area. Most of the outskirts of the citadel have been abandoned due to regular attacks from Darklands creatures, including hryngars, mongrelfolk, and worse. While a few stubborn souls eke out a living in the empty halls and corridors, most of the remaining population live in the citadel's nearly abandoned central keep. The mines that once provided the wealth of the Kravenkus have long since been played out, resulting in the departure of most of the populace to the Five Kings Mountains.⁠

Despite these hardships, the people of Kravenkus are proud of their home and refuse to seal the Darklands tunnels, viewing them as a connection to their life prior to the Quest for Sky. The dwarves welcome adventurers who offer assistance against the underground menaces.⁠
963608414:
Haeringar's Keep

Haeringar's Keep is the massive fortress of Haeringar the Everlasting. It is located in the Irriseni province of Feyfrost just south of the edge of the Winterwall Glacier. The fortress has enormous walls and 18 ice-encrusted stone towers which are patrolled by ice elementals. Haeringar's Keep was built there long before Baba Yaga's Winter War. Haeringar is an ancient fiendish frost giant oracle who is revered by the frost giants of Irrisen and Winterwall Glacier. Even the great Jarl Grungginnir of Holvirgang presents himself to him for counsel and blessings. Haeringar eats human flesh and is attended by a harem of ogresses. The gates of the fortress are always open but all the past adventurers, who have entered the keep trying to steal Haeringar's vast treasure, have failed.⁠
969377614:
Yllaldo Castle

Yllaldo Castle is a keep built atop a maze of tunnels in southern Xopatl. It is named for the legendary Arcadian hero-god Yllaldo the Manifester, who lived out the last of his years diligently guarding the keep until the end of the Age of Darkness.⁠
979681524:
Trollheim

The city of Trollheim can be found in Hagreach, the easternmost of the Linnorm Kingdoms, hard against its border with Irrisen and on the banks of the Rimeflow River. Trollheim has no current king and is ruled by Castellan Freyr Darkwine.⁠⁠⁠⁠
990464854:
Droskar's Crag

Droskar's Crag is an active volcano located in the Five Kings Range.⁠ The mountain consists of two primary peaks known as the Hammer and the Anvil. The Hammer reaches 28,822 feet in altitude, while the Anvil—which hosts the active crater known as Rovagug's Caldera—is 28,305 feet tall and grows by about one and a half feet per year. These heights make Droskar's Crag the tallest known active volcano on Golarion and the Five Kings Range's tallest mountain.⁠

Several rivers originate or are fed from glaciers on the Crag, including the Coldforge River (from the Coldforge glacier), the Slagiron River (from the Slagiron glacier), and the Goldmelt River (from the Gold glacier). The crag also hosts the East Gold, Sunset, Silver, Peakcrest, Eastrise, and Deaddrop glaciers.⁠

The volcano last erupted in 3980 AR in a massive explosion known as the Rending, which destroyed the capital of Tar Khadurrm at Jernashall⁠ and transformed the region. At the time Droskar's Crag was known as Torag's Crag; its name was changed after the Rending to reflect the more hostile nature of the volcano, since the evil dwarven god Droskar is the patron of endless toil and suffering. To date, it has shown no major activity, though the peaks constantly spew ash and smoke into the air as a constant reminder of the threat that exists beneath the snow-capped mountain.⁠⁠ Prior to the eruption that changed Torag's Crag into Droskar's Crag, this volcano had only one peak. The eruption in 3980 AR formed the two peaks of Droskar's Crag that are now known as Hammer and Anvil.⁠

In the centre is carved an ornate butterfly, the religious symbol of Desna, while in each corner of the platform stands a pillar. Regardless of these requirements, the results of Aalgin's rule has led to many positive changes in the area. These include the once-disgusting mire surrounding the town now being drinkable, and the town being protected from the elements by spruce canopies now interwoven to form a magical barrier.⁠

Alyssia's

Alyssia's is a very expensive but extremely beautiful teahouse in the Ivy District that caters to elven tastes and is run by Lady Alyssia. Lady Alyssia often calls on the Brotherhood of Abadar to deal with troublemakers and remove them from the premises.⁠

Whirlpool Rush

The Whirlpool Rush is a seaside cataract at the Nalt's Island in the Shackles. It is located on the eastern end of the straits between Redbow Isle and Nalt's Island. Sailors trying to avoid the hostile sedacthy-plagued waters of Shark Island, dare the straits between Redbow Isle and Nalt's Island and often meet their doom beneath the crashing waves of the whirlpool.⁠
1478035134:
Imvrildara

The ancient Calistrian temple of Imvrildara, located in the southern Fierani Forest of Kyonin, is the base for the goddess's most militant sect of worshipers: the Imvrildarai, defenders of the forest against Treerazer and its demonic armies.⁠
1479038074:
Nazilli

The ruins of the town of Nazilli are located on the southern edges of the Verduran Forest in Taldor.⁠⁠ The settlement was destroyed by the black dragon Aeteperax during a period of Taldan history known as the Dragon Plague.⁠
1481884484:

The monastic settlement of Tar Kuata, dedicated to the god Irori, is located among the peaks of the Barrier Wall in southwestern Osirion near the Footprints of Rovagug, and the borders of Thuvia and the Mwangi Expanse.⁠ The Monastery of Tar Kuata was founded by Narmek Tar Kuata, a Sothan priest of Irori now venerated as a saint.⁠

Many among the Pahmet, the sand dwarves, claim that Tar Kuata is home to some of their contemplative brethren, the Ouat, who are scholars of the martial arts taught in the monastery.⁠ The Ouat are in fact an isolated caste of dwarven monks based in the mountain valley near Tar Kuata.⁠ They are led by Menkha Helg.⁠

1506352604:
Katapesh Lodge

The Katapesh Lodge, the Pathfinder Society's local base of operations in the city of Katapesh, is an elegant three-tiered building located among cyclopean ruins and other ancient marvels in the Twilight Gate district. Venture-Captain Aurora Steelbloom oversees the operations of several teams of Pathfinders.⁠

The lodge maintains a library full of field agents' chapbooks, historical treatises, maps, rare tomes, and other items. The Pactmasters agreed to post two aluum outside the lodge for its protection. The building itself is thoroughly warded against any intrusion.⁠

There are three other lodges in Katapesh: Farseer Tower Lodge, Kotargo Lodge, and the Winding Road Lodge.

Beldrin's Tower, sometimes known as the Tower of the Broken Shield, is the most famous monument in the Precipice Quarter of Absalom. Originally part of a three-spire magic academy established by the wizard Beldrin, it suffered considerable damage after the earthquake of 4698 AR. It has since teetered on the cliff's edge, shaken and cracked but unbowed.⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠

Beldrin's Tower, as well as the shattered ruins of the other two towers, derive their name from the objects of power that Beldrin sequestered within: the Tower of the Candelabra for Beldrin's Candelabra, the Tower of the Horn for Beldrin's Horn, and the Tower of the Broken Shield for Beldrin's Shield.⁠⁠⁠ The three spires were also collectively known as the Tri-Towers, and the former name of the nearby Drownyard was the Tri-Towers Yard.⁠

Azurestone

The Galtan city of Azurestone takes its name from a the massive blue menhir that towers 100 feet above the town. Located on the plains north of the Boarwood, Azurestone has been relatively isolated from Galt's revolutionary fervour until recently. The stone is an object of religious reverence to the dwarves of the nearby Fog Peaks, who believe it to be a spear that was thrown down from Heaven in prehistoric times by their patron god Torag. These dwarves make regular pilgrimages to Azurestone, pumping up the local economy. Rumors of hidden chambers beneath the stone are beginning to attract adventurers and other undesirables to the city, who have also brought Galt's infamous revolutionary spirit with them.⁠

A trade route links the city with nearby Edme. Azurestone's patron deity is Erastil, but most of the benign gods are honoured by the citizens. The locals are mostly farmers and miners. Ordinarily, the city's location would make it subject to harsh winters, but these are mitigated by the influence of a relic known as the Vernal Key.⁠
1585315094:
Dortrot Ranch

Dortrot Ranch is a large horse ranch located on the plains of the eastern Gravelands just south of the Path River. The family of the owner, Chap "Old Man" Dortrot, has been raising both draft and warhorses there for 11 generations.⁠⁠
1589556854:
Xin-Haruka

Xin-Haruka was the capital of the Thassilonian kingdom of Haruka, dedicated to sloth. Its Runelords disregarded the mundane necessities of daily life and kept a multitude of servants and slaves who performed physical labor for them. The last Runelord of Sloth Krune, peacefully ascended the throne, succeeding Ivarinna and became the high priest of the goddess Lissala. A large number of summoned outsiders lived in the city, and a network of teleporters connected it to other regions or distant planes. Invisible servants kept the streets spotless and many kholos also lived in the city, serving in its armies, though their lazy nature did not make them good soldiers. The faiths of Lissala and the Peacock Spirit clashed in the streets, sometimes with oratory and other times with violence, and one of the largest temples dedicated to the goddess in Thassilon was located in the city. Several miles away, Desgard's Thousand Columns maintained a reserve of thousands of extraplanar soldiers that Krune could deploy in case of rebellion or external attack.⁠

The Moundlands, located near the confluence of the Whitegold and Vyalldehun Rivers, is where the early Linnorm Kings were buried. Serpent's Run is the largest building in Magnimar, quite a feat in the so-called city of monuments, and is located in one of the city's most prosperous areas, the Marble District. However, the late-summer rodeos sponsored by the Matador's Lodge are also held here.⁠

The arena is named for the carving of a gigantic serpent that runs around the upper rim of the arena, a tribute to the serpent slain by Alcaydian Indros. It is run by Master of Games Jorston "Axetongue" Droaeb.⁠

Cavern of the Sacred Shapes

The Cavern of the Sacred Shapes is a location in the Linnorm Kingdom of Icemark once used by the native Varki as a repository for their sculpture and other artwork. Several attempts have been made by more adventurous Varki to retake the Cavern, but all have failed. Kholo live in hide tents in the most sheltered areas, or dig burrows at the base of the canyon walls. Rath Sandstalker conducts frequent raids on caravans and small settlements, seeking healthy humanoids to sell at the Fleshfairs. The warriors of Fort Longjaw attempt an attack from time to time.⁠

The White Canyon tribe is the second-largest kholo hold in Katapesh.⁠

Despite the lingering fear many people have of the monstrous population here, kholo have not been a unified threat since the Siege of Solku, when the tribe assailed the city of Solku. 2147213884:
Flesh Block

Located in the commercial Downmarket district, the Flesh Block is Kaer Maga's slave market. Potential clients come here from all over Avistan, hoping to buy or sell the unusual sentient creatures the city attracts. The market also draws those wishing to sell themselves or their families into servitude, whether it is for limited indentured labor or into complete slavery. These voluntary sales are generally out of extreme necessity involving debt which would otherwise never be paid.⁠

Those being sold against their will can also be found at the Flesh Block. They are kept in large pens and sold off individually by professional auctioneers. These professionals not only sell people on commission, but also sometimes buy them in the hopes of fattening them up or otherwise improving their condition so that they may fetch a higher price later on.⁠

Even though it might seem contradictory at first, the Freemen of the Bottoms are frequent customers here. Having realized that they lack the military might to free all slaves within Kaer Maga, they hope to emancipate them legally after purchasing them.⁠
